name: Alba
text: Alba is the Gaelic name for northern Britain. Early texts also use the form Albu. From at least the ninth century, Fir Alba meant the Scots of Scotland. The term rí Alban named the king of the united Scots and Picts. Alba comes from the ancient attested name for Britain, *Albiòn. In heroic tales the name Alba usually points at all of Britain. The stricter sense, Pictland then Scotland, came later. The Welsh name Alba for Scotland appears in the fourteenth century. Cinaed mac Ailpín established Goidelic dominance in Scotland in 843. Gaelic then became the court tongue of the Scottish royal house.
